sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 30.07.2023 at about 2.00 p.m, the petitioner was doing his KEB work as a line man opposite to Thubarahalli Library, Kundalahalli - Varthur Kodi Junction, Bengaluru by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, at that time all of a sudden the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JS-9816 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life dashed to the petitioner.

entities.text: Thubarahalli Library, Kundalahalli - Varthur Kodi Junction
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to tremendous impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries & immediately shifted to Sakra Hospital for treatment wherein he underwent some clinical examinations and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He spent substantial amount towards his treatment.

Further at the time of accident he was hale and healthy and he was working as Line Man, BESCOM and getting a salary of Rs.75,000/-
p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he became disabled and lost his earning capacity.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. The respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JS-9816.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 147, 150, 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner who without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured,
the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 denied the negligence on his part but contended that the petitioner himself is the sole responsible for the accident.
The respondent No.2 admitted that he is the RC owner of the motorcycle and was duly insured with the 1 st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further submitted that rider of motorcycle was possess valid and effective driving licence.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES Vajramuni vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141969141/
2 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.07.2023 at about 2.00 p.m., Opposite to Thubarahalli Library,
Kundalahalli - Varthur Kodi Junction, M.N.Road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JS-9816 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

sentences.text:
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 19 were marked on his behalf.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 being the owner of the motorcycle examined himself as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
Further the respondent No.1 got examined the Officer as RW.2, Ex.R.4 & 5 was marked through him.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondents on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : From the evidence on record it is seen that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of the petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
9. In order to disprove the defence, the respondent No.2 being the owner of offending motorcycle himself was examined as RW.1.
RW.1 in his chief examination he reiterated the written statement averments.
During the course of his cross examination RW.1 stated that the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further he stated that his brother was riding the motorcycle at the time of accident.
Further he stated that he has not seen the accident.
He categorically admitted that accident occurred opposite to Thubarahalli Library and after the accident the police have seized the motorcycle.
He stated that police have given notice and in turn he was replied the same.
He admitted that as per Ex.P.9 his vehicle was damaged.
He stated that in his affidavit he stated that the petitioner was not crossing the road but he being the line man and was doing work.
He stated that due to the negligent act of the rider, the police have filed charge sheet against his vehicle rider.
This categorical admission also adds to the case of the petitioner.
Thus the unchallenged charge sheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle.
As such, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injury : Pain and swelling over left wrist.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary issued by Sakra Hospital, indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 30.07.2023 to 04.08.2023 (6 days in total).

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgery in the form of : CRIF with K-wire fixation - Left distal radius done under GA, Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
11. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the case of the petitioner that the accidental injuries have caused him permanent disability.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
12. Further during the course of his cross-examination the petitioner himself admitted that "At that time he was working as a lineman and he had a salary of Rs.70,000/- per month.
Further he stated that he was still working there and he was promoted to second class lineman.
Now His salary is Rs.80,000/-".

In view of the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439, in the case of Sri. Subash V/s The New India Ass.Co.Ltd and others, 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'

entities.text: Sri. Subash V/s The New India Ass.Co.Ltd and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The elicitations brought during the course of cross-examination of PW.1 also make it clear that he has not suffered any financial loss during his treatment period.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
13.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES: The period of hospitalization of 6 days
is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.7,200/- (1,200 X 6) is awarded under this head.
14. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
15. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P14, the petitioner has spent Rs.14,931/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Vajramuni vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141969141/
4 Rs.14,931/- which is rounded off to Rs.14,900/- towards medical expenses.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
17. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

18. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : - Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra : 7,200-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4
Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 5
Medical expenses : 14,900-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 1,22,100-00 19.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
20.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
21. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
